title: Embodied fly, stage 3c: the perturbation test on a well-traced leg: do the right hind leg's 25 claw neurons, closed through a servoed flybody leg, return a pushed tibia faster? (SIMULATED, closed loop)
status: registered before any closed-loop simulation of the hind leg
relation_to_parent: Stages 3a and 3b failed: feedback through the front leg's four claw neurons changed the motor neurons but not the leg, and the male CNS traces few front-leg proprioceptors. Stage 3c repeats stage 3b's perturbation test on the right hind leg, whose claw neurons are well traced (17 SNpp50 onto the tibia extensor motor neurons, 8 SNpp51 onto the tibia flexors), at the cost of a servoed body: flybody's hind-leg joints are position actuators, so feedback changes the commanded angle, not muscle force. Decision D19 in report/DECISION_LOG.md.
seen_before_registration: every stage-3a and 3b result; stage 2a (seeds 800-807): under forward-walking (BDN2, DNg100) drive the right hind tibia extensor pool fires tonically (median 34.12 Hz) and the flexor pool is silent

data only: right hind-leg claw neurons in the stage-1c network: SNpp50 (17) with direct synapses onto tibia extensor (131), trochanter flexor (74) and accessory tibia flexor (55) motor neurons; SNpp51 (8) onto sternotrochanter (218), pleural remotor (149), tibia flexor (86) motor neurons

body only (flybody, free joint removed, 0.01 ms step): the right hind tibia joint (tibia_T3_right, servo range -1.35 to 1.3, gain 0.4) is flexed by negative angles (claw to coxa 1.035 mm at -1.35, 2.135 mm at 1.3); held at 1.3, a 20 ms flexing torque of 0.1, 0.2, 0.4 gives an excursion of 0.213, 0.428, 0.852 rad and a return within 0.05 rad in 14, 20, 27 ms

design.network: the stage-1c male nerve cord (LIF, w_syn 0.275 mV), forward-walking drive (DNg100, both sides, 150 Hz)
design.body: flybody fruitfly.xml (commit d015e9b), free joint removed, 0.01 ms step; only tibia_T3_right is commanded, every other actuator held at 0
design.motor_map: right hind-leg motor neurons (vnc_motor, subclass hl, side R): extensor pool 'Ti extensor MN'; flexor pool 'Ti flexor MN' and 'Acc. ti flexor MN'; each pool's spikes filtered (tau 20 ms) into a mean rate, activation = rate / 20 Hz clipped to [0, 1]; net = extensor - flexor activation; command = net x 1.3 if net > 0, else |net| x -1.35; updated every 1 ms
design.feedback: the 25 right hind-leg claw neurons; theta = tibia angle, theta_0 = its value after the settle; extension-tuned rate = 150 Hz x clip((theta - theta_0) / (1.3 - theta_0), 0, 1); flexion-tuned = 150 Hz x clip((theta_0 - theta) / (theta_0 + 1.35), 0, 1); Poisson, suprathreshold (w_syn x 250), every 1 ms

arms.resistance: SNpp51 (onto the flexors) extension-tuned, SNpp50 (onto the extensor) flexion-tuned, perturbed
arms.sham: perturbed; each claw neuron receives its rate time course from the same seed's resistance_unperturbed trial

design.perturbation: a flexing torque of 0.3 on tibia_T3_right from 0.500 to 0.520 s
design.readouts: pre-pulse angle (median 0.40-0.50 s); excursion (pre-pulse angle minus the minimum 0.50-0.60 s); recovery time (ms after the pulse ends until the angle first returns to within 0.05 rad of the pre-pulse angle; the remaining time if never)

K0_the_leg_is_held_and_the_push_moves_it.statement: Precondition: open loop, the tibia is held extended and the push flexes it
K0_the_leg_is_held_and_the_push_moves_it.test: open-loop median pre-pulse angle >= 0.3 rad and median excursion >= 0.2 rad; if not, K1-K3 are uninterpretable

K1_feedback_speeds_the_return.statement: The resistance assignment returns the tibia faster than the open loop
K1_feedback_speeds_the_return.test: median recovery time in the resistance arm <= 0.8 x the open-loop median

K2_the_speed_needs_the_loop.statement: The faster return comes from feedback that follows the push
K2_the_speed_needs_the_loop.test: interpretable only if K1 passes: median recovery time in the resistance arm < the sham median

K3_the_opposite_assignment_does_not_spee.statement: The direction comes from which claw type carries which tuning
K3_the_opposite_assignment_does_not_spee.test: median recovery time in the assistance arm >= the open-loop median

not_claimed_even_if_all_pass: that the fly's resistance reflex runs this way: the leg is servoed, not muscle-driven; the tuning assignment is a stated bracket; one joint is commanded; a pass means the male-CNS wiring of the hind leg's claw neurons, closed through a simulated leg, returns a pushed tibia faster when SNpp51 carry extension, because of feedback that follows the push
reporting: Every prediction with its value and pass/fail or uninterpretable; per arm the pre-pulse angle, excursion, recovery time, tibia pool rates and claw rates.
